He, also, took an active part in student life, encouraged the college paper, and organized the College Band for the music of which he was responsible to the young ladies. After his year's work in Savoy he taught a year at the neighboring high school at Bells, then another two years in Alabama, before studying law and entering upon a successful career in that profession.

In the year, 1885-1886, another young man, Leonidas William McCown B.S., a native of Bowie, received the College's own training, came to the faculty as Professor of English and Literature. As a student in the College he had received his degree in 1885. This interest he continued during his career as teacher.

During the last four years of the College's operation, after 1886, the management was placed in the hands of the staff of the Plainsman Messenger in the spring of 1888. For the second year of his administration Professor Halbell, Natural Sciences, Professor Pritchett having returned to the work of Modern Languages, was added to the faculty. He entered the Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, at Louisville, graduated in 1892, and later went out to serve as missionary in China.

When Professor Holland left the chair of Mathematics in early 1887, Elihu R. Hinshaw, a native of Indiana, came to the faculty, first as Professor of Natural and Applied Mathematics, later as Professor of Mathematics and Natural Science, and Treasurer, and the associate editor of the College paper. Mr. Hinshaw had received the A.B. degree in 1882, was considerably older than the other faculty members.
